title: Evaluation of cutaneous temperature and electrolyte measurement in sweat and sensor-based motion analysis in patients with liver disease
summary:
Patients with an increased risk of hepatic encephalopathy (HE) receive an adhesive sensor for regular sweat-based measurement of blood salts and temperature as well as a sensor for motion analysis upon admission to the hospital. In parallel, regular blood samples (ca 3x/week) and psychometric tests for HE diagnostics are taken during the inpatient stay.
The aim of the study is 1. whether HE can be predicted from the movement pattern recorded and 2.to determine whether the adhesive sensor-based measurements correspond to the standard of blood sampling and laboratory analysis.

interventions.name:
hourly cutaneous patch based mesurement of K+, Na2+ and temperature 
+ continuous UWB based motion analysis
+ regular blood sampling (3x/week)
+ daily clinical hepatic enzaphalopathy assessment

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
patients hospitalized on the MK1-S4 ward in UKDD with increased HE risk:
Age >18, Informed Consent possible
Confirmed liver cirrhosis or
Portosystemic shunt (TIPS, traumatic, portal vein thrombosis/compression) or
Acute liver failure
Exclusion criteria:
Not capable of giving informed consent and no authorized representative
No knowledge of the German or English language
Severe cognitive impairment of a different origin
Patch allergy or extensive skin damage/infection
Diseases with impairment of the sweat glands (cystic fibrosis/Sjögren's/scleroderma)
Known hyperhidrosis
Photosensitive epilepsy
Pregnancy
